title: Vector and Static
premise: Bram Kavanagh, a clone created to settle the murdered original's estate, arrives on the dying colony of Meridian's Rest expecting paperwork and finds a community of forgotten people who treat him as both heir and impostor. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, Bram discovers the original was investigating the flicker's source—a derelict relay broadcasting an inheritance signal meant for clones like him. Racing corporate salvagers to the relay at the edge of dead space, Bram must choose between erasing his clone status to claim a human identity or preserving the signal that will save the colony. He transmits the colony's existence outward, accepting that belonging is something built, not inherited.
about_author: Mirabel Amberdale is a former radio archivist who spent six years cataloguing abandoned transmission logs from decommissioned deep-space relays. She writes quiet, melancholy science fiction about people left behind by progress.

chapters.title: The Estate of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Bram Kavanagh arrives on Meridian's Rest to settle his original's estate, carrying legal papers and a face everyone recognizes. The colonists watch him with open hostility and grief. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: alienation—he is a stranger wearing a beloved man's skin.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds; crops lift, water hangs, then everything crashes down. The colonists blame Bram's arrival as an omen. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: dread—the world itself has become untrustworthy.

chapters.title: What the Original Left Behind
chapters.summary: Sorting the original's belongings, Bram finds encrypted research notes about gravitational anomalies and a map to a relay in dead space. Sefa, the original's former partner, warns him to burn it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance—curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: The Colony That Forgot Itself
chapters.summary: Bram tours the failing settlement: cracked domes, a shuttered school, elders who remember when supply ships came yearly instead of never. Young Toma asks if Bram remembers him—the original promised to fix the water reclaimers. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: guilt for debts he didn't incur but now owns.

chapters.title: Corporate Shadows
chapters.summary: A survey vessel from Halcyon Extraction enters orbit, officially 'assessing salvage value.' Its liaison, Director Oyelaran, interviews Bram about the original's final weeks with unsettling precision. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: paranoia—the murder case may have powerful interested parties.

chapters.title: Sefa's Grief
chapters.summary: Sefa finally speaks to Bram alone, confessing she and the original had decoded part of the anomaly: the nine-second flicker is periodic, and it's getting stronger. She hates Bram for existing yet needs what he knows. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: grief tangled with resentment toward a copy of the man she lost.

chapters.title: Decoding the Dead
chapters.summary: Bram and Sefa crack the original's encryption together, finding recordings of the original's investigation—and his growing conviction that someone killed him for it. The last entry names the relay coordinates. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: intimacy with a dead man through his own voice.

chapters.title: The Murder Case Reopened
chapters.summary: Bram formally reopens the death investigation, forcing the colonial administration to release sealed evidence: the original's shuttle telemetry shows tampering before his fatal 'accident.' POV: Bram. Emotional beat: resolve—grief converted into purpose.

chapters.title: Oyelaran's Offer
chapters.summary: Director Oyelaran offers Bram citizenship papers, full legal personhood, and passage off-world—in exchange for the relay data. Bram realizes Halcyon wants the flicker's source buried. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation—identity offered as a bribe.

chapters.title: Riot at the Reclaimer
chapters.summary: Halcyon crews begin stripping colony infrastructure as 'abandoned assets.' A protest turns violent; Toma is injured defending the water reclaimers. Bram publicly sides with the colonists. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: solidarity—the clone chooses the forgotten over the powerful.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Monitoring the flicker cycle, Sefa isolates a structured signal inside the gravitational noise—an inheritance broadcast aimed at registered clones. It's addressed to Bram's genetic line specifically. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: awe and unease—the dead are still talking.

chapters.title: The Clone Registry
chapters.summary: Bram hacks the colonial registry and learns he is not the only Kavanagh clone: three others exist, scattered across the system, all contacted by the signal. One responded—and went silent. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: vertigo—brothers he never knew, one possibly dead.

chapters.title: Preparations for Dead Space
chapters.summary: The colonists secretly refit the original's old long-range skiff while Halcyon watches the spaceport. Sefa insists on coming; Toma stows away. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: fragile hope—a community investing its future in a clone it resented.

chapters.title: Departure Window
chapters.summary: During the next gravity flicker, when Halcyon's sensors blind themselves, the skiff slips orbit. Oyelaran launches pursuit within minutes. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the knowledge there's no going back.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Weeks in transit through dead space: rationing, silence, Toma's fever, and Bram confronting memories implanted from the original that surface like ghosts. Sefa teaches him which memories were truly his own. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: mourning the self he borrowed.

chapters.title: Brother Static
chapters.summary: They find the silent clone—Kavanagh-3—adrift in a gutted ship near the relay, barely alive. Before losing consciousness he warns: Halcyon reached the relay first and left a trap. POV: Kavanagh-3 (fragmented). Emotional beat: recognition—meeting yourself as a stranger.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: They approach the ancient relay, a pre-colonial artifact older than any chart, humming with the flicker's source frequency. Halcyon's trap—a proximity mine field—forces a desperate manual threading run. POV: Toma. Emotional beat: terror transformed into courage.

chapters.title: What the Original Discovered
chapters.summary: Inside the relay, Bram accesses the archive: the flicker is a distress pulse from a fleet of generation ships lost centuries ago, and the original died proving the colony sits on their rescue corridor. Halcyon knew. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: fury—the murder was silencing salvation.

chapters.title: Halcyon Arrives
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's ship docks, offering Bram everything again—personhood, wealth, erasure of his clone record—if he deletes the archive. Behind her, Halcyon marines board. Sefa triggers the relay's defenses. POV: Oyelaran. Emotional beat: cold pragmatism meeting something it cannot price.

chapters.title: Climax: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Under fire, Bram physically couples the archive to the relay's transmitter during the strongest flicker yet, sending the rescue corridor's coordinates to every listening point in the system—including the lost fleet's descendants. Kavanagh-3 dies holding the connection open. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrifice—identity given meaning through action, not paperwork.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: The flicker resolves into steady, gentle pulses as response signals arrive from the lost ships' children. Halcyon withdraws under public exposure. On Meridian's Rest, the colonists greet Bram not as the original or a copy, but by his own name. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning.

chapters.title: Vector and Static
chapters.summary: Months later, rescue vessels fill the sky and the colony rebuilds around the relay. Bram files no citizenship petition; instead he registers a new identity entirely his own, co-signed by Sefa and Toma. Standing beneath returning ships, he finally belongs—to a future, not a past. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: homecoming—belonging chosen, not inherited.
